name: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab
role: Arab Muslim scholar, theologian and reformer
contribution: An Arab Muslim scholar, theologian, preacher, activist, religious leader, jurist, and reformer, who was from Najd in the Arabian Peninsula and is considered as the eponymous founder of the Wahhabi movement.
legacy: He promoted strict adherence to Islamic law, proclaiming the necessity of returning directly to the Quran and Hadith literature rather than relying on traditional interpretations, and insisted that every Muslim – male and female – should personally read and study the Quran.

checks.lead: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Sulayman al-Tamimi al-Najdi (Arabic: مُحَمَّد بن عبد الوهاب بن سليمان التميمي النجدي, romanized: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Sulaymān at-Tamīmī al-Najdī; 1703–1792 C.E., 1115–1206 A.H.) was an Arab Muslim scholar, theologian, preacher, activist, religious leader, jurist, and reformer, who was from Najd in the Arabian Peninsula and is considered as the eponymous founder of the Wahhabi movement.
